walkthrough:
Differentiate $f(x) = \frac{1}{3}(2x - 1)^{3/2} - 2x$ with respect to $x$ using the chain rule:
$$f'(x) = \frac{1}{3} \times \frac{3}{2}(2x - 1)^{1/2} \times 2 - 2 = (2x - 1)^{1/2} - 2 = \sqrt{2x - 1} - 2$$

Square both sides to solve the inequality for $x$:
$$2x - 1 \le 4 \implies 2x \le 5 \implies x \le \frac{5}{2}$$

State the maximum possible value of the constant $a$:
$$a = \frac{5}{2} \quad (\text{or } 2.5)$$

ai_rubric.Increasing and Decreasing Functions: Differentiates correctly to $(2x - 1)^{1/2} - 2$ (B2). Sets $(2x - 1)^{1/2} - 2 \le 0$ and squares (M1). Obtains $a = \frac{5}{2}$ (A1).
